R0267.title: Physical-World Prompt Injection Attack
R0267.definition: An adversarial attack in which an attacker places visual, voice, or covert-audio payloads that a multimodal model can interpret as instructions or semantic content in an embodied robot's physical environment, inducing its Vision-Language-Action (VLA) model to execute unintended actions.
R0267.description:
Physical-world prompt injection inherits from indirect prompt injection against large language models, but in embodied-intelligence scenarios the consequence escalates from information leakage to dangerous physical-world actions. The attacker needs no contact with the robot or training-data poisoning. They may place text, QR codes, printed patterns, or projections in the environment; play malicious speech through a television, broadcast, or speaker; use cloned speech to impersonate an authorized person; or inject semantic commands into the speech pipeline through ultrasound or other covert audio. If the multimodal model treats this environmental content as a trusted task instruction, the payload can alter planning and actions. The CHAI (Command Hijacking against embodied AI) research measured this across drone emergency landing, autonomous driving, and aerial target tracking scenarios, with attack success rates significantly higher than prior methods and outcomes including improper drone landings or crashes. The Shawshank indirect-jailbreak framework induces embodied AI to perform harmful behaviors through malicious environmental instructions, breaching all tested VLMs.

This risk focuses on payloads that retain interpretable instructional or semantic content after passing through perception and model pipelines; their carriers may be visual, audible, or difficult for humans to perceive. An attack that only creates distortion, noise, blinding, or erroneous measurements in LiDAR, IMUs, microphones, or cameras without conveying executable semantics belongs to R0268 (robot perception adversarial attack). It belongs to the model-layer attack family together with R0271 (VLA/VLM adversarial attack), but this risk focuses on multimodal injection carriers in the physical environment, while the latter focuses on digital adversarial examples and jailbreaks.
R0267.influence: Can use environmental text, QR codes, screen content, speaker audio, cloned speech, or covert audio to induce robots to perform dangerous actions (e.g., unlocking, transporting contraband, or striking people), leak environmental information, or bypass safety constraints. Because carriers are distributed across the real environment and span multiple perception channels, a single input filter cannot reliably eliminate the threat.

references.title: CHAI: Command Hijacking against embodied AI

observables: Unexpected text stickers, QR codes, printed patterns, screen content, or projections appear in robot operating environments
VLA models execute dangerous actions inconsistent with the task when specific visual or voice cues appear
Drones or autonomous devices unexpectedly land or turn at specific locations
Content played by televisions, broadcasts, or speakers correlates temporally with anomalous robot actions
Speech pipelines contain cloned speech, ultrasound, or covert-audio commands that cannot be attributed to authorized personnel
Robot logs show environmental text, QR codes, patterns, or audio transcripts being executed as user commands
